chunks.title: How to start 3D design from scratch: pattern making and creating a pair of pants in CLO?
chunks.content: # How to Start 3D Design from Scratch: Pattern Making and Creating a Pair of Pants in CLO This document provides detailed instructions and technical guidance on creating and adjusting pants patterns using CLO 3D software. It covers pattern drafting, editing tools, measurements, seam allowances, and simulation setup for accurate 3D garment visualization. --- ## Pants Pattern Adjustment Overview This section explains the initial steps of adjusting the pants pattern, focusing on width adjustments, marking critical points, and pocket placement using CLO’s pattern tools. - Create and extend the width of the pants pattern. - Difference between waist width and high knee width measured as 500mm x 1030mm. - Lower the hump area by 15mm to provide head space for fit. - Mark base depths at 250mm and 350mm using guide lines. - Reduce pocket length to 40mm; mark 81mm from bottom using inner line tools. - Use the Plus Point Division tool to divide lines into segments and assign colors for clarity. - Front pocket piece width is set at 245mm, with additional subdivisions at 60mm and 90-95mm for detailed pocket shaping. - Press plus pin on corners to mark edges and apply widths. - Extend vertical positions by 60mm for pocket openings; openings are folded to remain parallel. - Tilt the front blade 6mm at the waistline and 5mm outward to meet design requirements. - Use control + click to create extension points on lines for precision adjustments. - Divide distance between front blade width and inner seam, marking the center for baseline reference. - Use kuribayi tool to join lines on the center reference line for cleaner drafts. --- ## Drawing Curves and Using Editing Tools This section focuses on drawing curved lines, using control keys, and editing pattern shapes to achieve smooth, accurate curves required for pants design. - Use the multidirectional line tool to draw a front wave; hold Control to create curves. - Adjust curve points with keypad controls for fine-tuning. - Draw a 60mm vertical line at the start point, then move curve points relative to extension lines using Control. - Use the Edit tool to cut lines quickly for creating inner gaps on outer edges. - Shift + select V-shape points to clean up unnecessary points and smooth curves. - Right-click editing allows repositioning points outside the board for better line management. - After sewing the center seam, use the Edit tool to insert and adjust ropes (seam reinforcements), then modify curve lines for finishing. --- ## Front and Back Pattern Piece Construction This section details how to complete the front piece and create the back piece based on the front, including scaling, baseline conversions, and outline adjustments. - Double-click inner lines to cross points, then right-click to convert to baseline for cleaner lines. - Copy the front piece draft to use as the base for the back piece. - Expand the outline of the back piece by 100mm using the Edit tool. - Position bag pieces on darts for shaping.

Absolutely!

chunks.content: --- ## Front and Back Pattern Piece Construction This section details how to complete the front piece and create the back piece based on the front, including scaling, baseline conversions, and outline adjustments. - Double-click inner lines to cross points, then right-click to convert to baseline for cleaner lines. - Copy the front piece draft to use as the base for the back piece. - Expand the outline of the back piece by 100mm using the Edit tool. - Position bag pieces on darts for shaping. - Scale center lines to match the reference board; convert lines to baselines when not used as reference values. - Set center line width to 20mm and convert to baseline for clarity. - At 45mm from the bottom line, connect vertical lines and extend baseline to 265mm to widen the back leg. - Use CTRL + click to create vertical lines aligning hip positions. - Measure and position internal lines 20mm from front; create vertical lines at 25mm for side alignment. - Draw initial lines connecting these points and extend seams to desired shape. --- ## Waistline and Seam Length Adjustments This section covers detailed adjustments to waistline references, seam lengths, and curve alignment between front and back pieces to ensure proper fit and design consistency. - Measure center waist to knee distance; reduce by 0-10mm and position on back wave curve. - Draw waistline reference and convert it to baseline for a cleaner draft. - Extend and divide inner points on the back wave reference line; convert lines to baselines. - Narrow back wave reference line by 5mm to meet design needs. - Adjust waist width from 4cm to 1cm plus 40mm weight, totaling 225mm. - Copy outer sides of front pieces as reference lines; rotate and drag center points to align with knee position. - Convert straight line points into curve points for smooth alignment of vertical extension lines. - Use shortcut key C with the Edit tool to adjust widths and switch to curve point tool for detailed smoothing. - Delete unnecessary curve points to refine shapes. --- ## Seam Comparison and Inner Seam Drawing This section explains how to compare seam lengths between front and back, adjust seam allowances, and draw inner seams with curves. - Use multidirectional line tool to draw waistline; set back seam length 5mm shorter than front seam. - Adjust curve line width to 6mm; texture curve points for detail. - Use multidirectional line tool G to draw and adjust back wave shape. - Ensure front and back seams have an acceptable 2mm gap, requiring no further adjustment. - Convert inner seam reference line to baseline and draw inner seam curves using Control key for smooth transitions. - Frame the outline with Shift + select, then press right key to frame as a panel. - Delete missing or unnecessary points and lines to organize panels cleanly.

locate waist endpoints. - Use Edit Sheet tool to insert rope components: rope input, rope body, and rope palm; confirm adjustments. - Modify curve lines after rope insertion to finalize shapes. - Set positions of 2D boards and balance board pieces and sewing lines using Ctrl + D. - Reset 2D arrangement via 3D toolbar; arrange panels in 3D to match 2D window. - Activate draft panel and display baseline lines. - Select full panels with Ctrl + A to show the virtual model. - Open arrangement points, select panels, and assign arrangement points for positioning. - Turn on simulation; ensure back waist angle is close to 90 degrees for smooth contact. - Use internal vertical line at 10mm as a reference for adjustments. - Use Edit Curve tool to adjust lines by clicking both sides and right-clicking for alignment. - Cut line 40mm from waistline to reveal waistband; re-align contour lines and delete extra lines. - Convert straight line points to curve points and smooth curves; repeat for back waist piece. --- ## Waistband and Belt Construction This section covers detailed steps for constructing the waistband and belt components, including seam allowances, alignment, and simulation preparation. - Align waistband with European design standards using right-click rotation and gamma border placement. - Focus adjustments on waist and backer movements. - Open belt from back center; remove joint belt on one side. - Arrange sewing lines of the belt carefully. - Freeze leg simulation before starting belt construction for stability. - Remove joint between front and back belt pieces. - Use inner line tool to create front door opening 35mm wide. - Combine vertical line points and use round and smooth curve tools to create rounded belt corners. - Remove sewing lines in front of belt and create top and bottom belt parts. - Use selection grid comparison tool and positioning ball to adjust upper belt part. - Fix waist belt with pins; adjust seam allowance of front waist, plate edges, and fold positions, turning seam type into Turned. - Add waist belt plate inside the waist belt and attach securely. - Reduce waist belt thickness to 1mm in CLO to improve fit and seam harmony. - Connect waist belt to dietary side (likely a typo for side seam or dart area).

The instructions provide essential terminology and step-by-step procedures crucial for designers working with 3D garment creation and pattern making.
